332342.title: Binary single-\diamond universal partial word existence conjecture
332342.statement: Let $A={0,1}$, let $n\binom{}{}\geq 1$, and consider linear upwords for $A^n$ containing a single $\Diamond$ at position $k$. The cases covered by Theorem~ are $k=n$ for $n\geq 2$, while the additional cases covered by Theorem~ are $n=3$, $k=4$, and $n=4$, $k\in\{5,7\}$. **Binary single-$\Diamond$ existence conjecture.** For $A=\{0,1\}$ and any $n\geq 1$, there is a linear upword for $A^n$ containing a single $\Diamond$ at position $k$ in every case not covered by Theorem~ or Theorem~. Equivalently, the preceding non-existence cases are the only ones for a binary alphabet with a single $\Diamond$. This conjecture asserts existence in all remaining parameter cases after the stated small cases and the case $k=n$ have been excluded.

332965.title: Bhattacharya–Weitsman–Nadirashvili sharp quantitative Faber–Krahn conjecture
332965.statement:
Let $N\geq 2$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be an open bounded set. Denote by $\lambda(\Omega)$ the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of the Laplacian on $\Omega$, let $B$ be a ball, and let $\mathcal{A}(\Omega)$ be the Fraenkel asymmetry of $\Omega$.

**Bhattacharya–Weitsman–Nadirashvili conjecture.** There exists a dimensional constant $C>0$ such that

$$
|\Omega|^{2/N}\,\lambda(\Omega)-|B|^{2/N}\,\lambda(B)\geq \frac{1}{C}\,\mathcal{A}(\Omega)^2.
$$

This conjecture asks for a sharp quantitative refinement of the Faber–Krahn inequality, asserting that the eigenvalue deficit controls the squared Fraenkel asymmetry. The source presents it as a conjecture of Bhattacharya and Weitsman and, independently, Nadirashvili; no resolution is supplied here.

333201.title: Strong spanning subdigraphs in highly arc-strong and arc-antistrong digraphs
333201.statement:
Let $D$ be a digraph. It is **$k$-arc-strong** when deleting fewer than $k$ arcs leaves a strongly connected digraph, and **$k$-arc-antistrong** when deleting fewer than $k$ arcs leaves an antistrong digraph.

**Special-case conjecture.** There exists a natural number $k$ such that every digraph $D$ which is both $k$-arc-strong and $k$-arc-antistrong has arc-disjoint strong spanning subdigraphs $D_1,D_2$.

This is proposed as a potentially easier special case of the preceding connectivity conjecture. The supplied text gives no resolution, so its status is open.

333364.title: The augmented-weighing conjecture for counterfeit coin strategies
333364.statement: Let $t=fk+r$, where $k$ and $r$ are positive integers, $0<r<f$, and $k\geq 4$. Split the coins into groups $A_1,\ldots,A_f$, $B_1,\ldots,B_f$, and $C_1,\ldots,C_f$, with $|A_i|=k-2$ and $|B_i|=1$, $|C_i|=2$ for $1\leq i\leq r$, and $|A_i|=k-3$, $|B_i|=2$, $|C_i|=1$ for $r+1\leq i\leq f$. The strategy compares sums of groups within the index intervals $[1,r]$ and $[r+1,f]$. **The augmented-weighing conjecture.** If $\left\lfloor\dfrac{t}{f}\right\rfloor\geq 4$ and either $0<d<f$ or $d$ is not of the form $qf$ or $qf\pm r$ for some positive integer $q$, there exists a successful counterfeit-coin strategy.

333477.title: Bárány–Larman colored Tverberg conjecture
333477.statement:
Let $F_1,\ldots,F_{d+1}$ be families of $r$ points each in $\mathds{R}^d$, considered as color classes. A **colorful partition** is a partition into $r$ sets $A_1,\ldots,A_r$ such that each part has exactly one point of each color. **Bárány–Larman's colored Tverberg conjecture.** There is a colorful partition such that

$$
\bigcap_{j=1}^r \operatorname{conv}(A_j)\neq\emptyset.
$$

This is a long-standing open problem concerning a colorful analogue of Tverberg's theorem.

333510.title: Sunflower conjecture in $(\mathbb Z/D\mathbb Z)^n$
333510.statement:
Let $k\leq D$, and let $A\subset(\mathbb Z/D\mathbb Z)^n$. A collection of vectors is a **$k$-sunflower** if, in every coordinate, its entries are either all different or all equal; $A$ is $k$-sunflower-free if it contains no such collection. **Sunflower conjecture in $(\mathbb Z/D\mathbb Z)^n$.** There is a constant $b_k$, depending only on $k$, such that

$$
|A|\leq b_k^n.
$$

For $k=3$ and $D=3$, the sunflower condition is equivalent to being a three-term arithmetic progression in $\mathbb F_3^n$. The paper gives bounds for the three-sunflower case, while the stated conjecture remains open.

333533.title: Ziegler–Alon–Drewnowski–Łuczak conjecture on stable Kneser hypergraphs
333533.statement:
Let $k$, $r$, and $n$ be positive integers with $n\geq rk$ and $r\geq2$. An $r$-stable $k$-element subset of $\{1,\dots,n\}$ is one in which any two elements have cyclic distance at least $r$. The hypergraph $\mathrm{KG}^r(k,n)_{r\text{-stab}}$ is the subhypergraph of the $r$-uniform Kneser hypergraph induced by these $r$-stable subsets.

**Ziegler–Alon–Drewnowski–Łuczak conjecture.**

$$
\chi\bigl(\mathrm{KG}^r(k,n)_{r\text{-stab}}\bigr)=\left\lceil\frac{n-r(k-1)}{r-1}\right\rceil.
$$

The source attributes this conjecture to Ziegler, Alon, Drewnowski, and Łuczak. The supplied text does not give evidence that it has been resolved.

4\leq r\leq q,

$$
t_r(A_r)=2.

334104.title: The dynamic coloring conjecture for planar graphs
334104.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph, let $r$ be a positive integer, and let $\chi_r^d(G)$ denote the least number of colors in an $r$-dynamic coloring of $G$.

**Dynamic coloring conjecture.**

$$
\chi_r^d(G) \le \begin{cases} r+3 & \text{if }1\le r \le2 \\\ r+5& \text{if }3\le r \le7 \\ \lfloor\frac{3r}{2}\rfloor +1 & \text{if } r \ge8. \\\end{cases}
$$

This conjecture concerns the number of colors needed for dynamic colorings of planar graphs and is analogous to conjectures for ordinary colorings of planar graphs. The supplied text does not indicate whether it has been resolved.

334132.title: Third-page stabilization conjecture for plane-curve spectral sequences
334132.statement:
Let $C:f=0$ be any reduced plane curve, and let $E_r^{s,t}(f)_k$ denote the terms of the spectral sequences associated with $C$. Let $d$ be the degree of $C$, let $k$ be an integer in $[1,d]$, and let $t=0,1,2$.

$$
\dim E_{3}^{2-t,t}(f)_k=\dim E_{\infty}^{2-t,t}(f)_k.

334219.title: Planar triangulations admit paired total dominating color classes
334219.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar triangulation with at least four vertices. A **proper $4$-coloring** of $G$ is a partition of its vertices into four independent color classes $(C_1,C_2,C_3,C_4)$, and a **total dominating set** is a vertex set whose every vertex has a neighbor in the set.

**Four-color extension conjecture.** Every planar triangulation with at least four vertices has a proper $4$-coloring $(C_1,C_2,C_3,C_4)$ such that both $C_1\cup C_2$ and $C_3\cup C_4$ are total dominating sets.

This would provide a structured strengthening of the two-set conclusion for planar triangulations. The paper says that computer search suggests the statement, while only particular cases are established.

334705.title: He and Ye's free-vertex conjecture for 4-regular 4-uniform hypergraphs
334705.statement:
Let $H$ be a **4-regular 4-uniform hypergraph**, meaning that every edge has four vertices and every vertex belongs to four edges. A **free vertex** is a vertex $v$ such that $V(H)\setminus\{v\}$ can be $2$-colored so that every edge contains vertices of both colors, with $v$ uncolored.

**He and Ye's free-vertex conjecture.** Every $4$-regular $4$-uniform hypergraph contains a free vertex.

337410.title: The incremental conjecture for set multipartite Ramsey numbers

$$
M_s(n+1)\leq M_s(n)+1.
$$
 The preceding proposition proves this bound under an additional numerical hypothesis; the conjecture asserts that the hypothesis can be removed.

337517.title: Pendent-path transfer conjecture for adjacent attachment vertices
337517.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph, and let $u$ and $v$ be adjacent vertices of $G$ with degree at least $2$. Let $G_{p,q}(u,v)$ denote the graph obtained by attaching pendent paths of lengths $p$ and $q$ at $u$ and $v$, respectively, and let $\rho_{\alpha}$ be the alpha-index. **Pendent-path transfer conjecture.** If $\alpha\in[0,1)$, $q\geq1$, and $p\geq q+2$, then

$$
\rho_{\alpha}\left(G_{p,q}(u,v)\right)<\rho_{\alpha}\left(G_{p-1,q+1}(u,v)\right).
$$

337830.title: The $(1,1,2,2,2,2)$ and $(1,1,2,2,2)$ coloring conjecture for cubic graphs
337830.statement:
A **cubic graph** is a graph in which every vertex has degree three, and a **3-edge-colorable cubic graph** is a cubic graph whose edges admit a proper coloring with three colors. An $S$-coloring, for a sequence $S=(s_1,\dots,s_k)$, is a coloring of the edges with colors $1,\dots,k$ such that edges of color $i$ are pairwise at distance at least $s_i+1$; the graph is $S$-colorable when such a coloring exists.

**$(1,1,2,2,2,2)$ and $(1,1,2,2,2)$ coloring conjecture.** Every cubic graph is $(1,1,2,2,2,2)$-colorable, and every 3-edge-colorable cubic graph is $(1,1,2,2,2)$-colorable.

The conjecture is proposed as an extension of results previously proved for a subclass of cubic graphs. The supplied text does not give a proof or resolution.

381332.title: Sheehan's conjecture on uniquely Hamiltonian regular graphs
381332.statement:
A finite graph is **$r$-regular** if every vertex has degree $r$, and a **Hamilton cycle** is a cycle containing every vertex of the graph exactly once.

**Sheehan's conjecture.** There is no finite $r$-regular graph with a unique Hamilton cycle for any $r>2$.

This conjecture concerns whether uniqueness of a Hamilton cycle can occur in finite regular graphs of degree greater than two. It is still open, although partial results have been proved.
